newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand bounced off its weakest levels in choppy trade towards the close on Wednesday, but ended the day over one cent below its previous finish.
Dealers said the currency had been volatile during the afternoon, moved around by London banks amid a dearth of local influence.

"Most of the stuff was from London banks. There was demand which took (the rand) well above the 4.43 level and then selling there which brought it quickly back down to around 4.4270," one dealer said.
"It is trying to find a clear direction which is the reason why it has been all over the place."
Traders said activity was largely speculative and local corporate involvement minimal.
The rand ended the session at 4.4260/4290 on the dollar from 4.4145/4175 close Tuesday, after bouncing between the 4.4340 and 4.4250 levels for most of the afternoon.
Dealers predicted a trading range of 4.4200-4.4350 on Thursday "unless there is any big news to throw it out".
Activity was expected to be quiet, characterised by position-squaring ahead of the long weekend. Markets will be closed on Friday to celebrate the Human Rights Day holiday.
Against the crosses, the rand was last quoted at 7.0781/0873 against sterling from 7.0014/0106 at the close on Tuesday and at 0.3796/3800 marks from 0.3809/3812 previously.

On the bond market securities held firmer levels in late afternoon in sporadic trade, ignoring weaker U.S. Treasuries which erased their earlier gains following slightly higher-than-expected consumer inflation.
Dealers said there was "gentle" buying in the long end of the South African market throughout the day from both local and foreign players, although selling was seen in the shorter side.
They said some short-covering had also been seen, spilling over from the U.S. market.

"Some people expected the (U.S.) T-bond to go over seven percent if the CPI was bad and they went short on this. When it didn't go (above seven) there was a rush to cover. I think that mindset carried over into our market," a dealer said.

U.S. February CPI, released at 1330 GMT, showed a 0.3 percent monthly rise, a touch higher than forecasts for a 0.2 percent increase causing the 30-year T-bond to move up to 6.97 percent from 6.95 earlier.
At 1415 GMT the key R150 bond was yielding 15.055 percent from 15.140 overnight and just off a day's best of 15.015 percent.
Dealers said bonds were seen trading in a 14.95-15.10 percent range on Thursday with trade quiet before the long weekend.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates held steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate maintained its recent 15.90 to 16.10 percent range.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage continued edging higher, rising to 9.918 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.896 billion on Monday.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners turned sellers of bonds on Tuesday offloading a net 129.05 million rand's worth of bonds after buying 839.48 million rand's worth on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market amounted to 9.13 billion rand on Tuesday compared with 5.52 billion on Monday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
